title: Why EVs Hide Their Battery in the FLOOR 🛹🔋 #shorts

scenes.text: Why do almost all electric cars put the battery in the floor? Meet the skateboard platform.
Lift off the body: a flat battery slab between the axles, motors at the wheels. Almost any body fits on top.
A typical pack weighs about a thousand pounds. Mounted low, it drags the center of gravity down.
So EVs resist tipping. In federal tests, the Tesla Model Y scored a seven point nine percent rollover risk, then the lowest of any SUV.
No engine, no driveshaft tunnel: a flat floor, more cabin room, often a front trunk.
Newer designs make the battery case part of the floor itself. Stiffer body, fewer parts.
The heaviest part does three jobs. What else could pull double duty? Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
